title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: q: S -> T is a relative scheme and E is an O_S-module, probably quasi-coherent; the image seems to read 'qu. coh.' rather than 'loc. libre'. The first-order principal parts give the jet exact sequence (1): 0 -> E⊗Ω^1_{S/T} -> P^1_{S/T}(E) -> E -> 0. This is an extension of O_S-modules.

The universal first-order differential operator d^1_E: E -> P^1_{S/T}(E), x ↦ 1⊗x, splits (1). The splitting is additive and q^{-1}(O_T)-linear but not O_S-linear. Using it, every section of P^1(E) is written uniquely as ξ = d^1_E x + ω, with x a section of E and ω a section of E⊗Ω^1.

The page computes the O_S-module structure in these coordinates. Write f·d^1_E x = d^1_E(fx) + (f - d^1(f))·d^1_E(x). Here f - d^1 f = -df, and multiplying by d^1_E x only sees x modulo the ideal. This gives (4): f(d^1_E x + ω) = d^1_E(fx) + (fω - x⊗df).

A connection δ_E of E relative to T is defined as an O_S-linear splitting of (1). Comparing it with the additive splitting d^1_E, it is determined by an additive map d^0_E: E -> E⊗Ω^1_{S/T} via (6): δ_E x = d^1_E x - d^0_E x.

The page ends by asking for the condition on d^0_E making δ_E O_S-linear. The next page derives the Leibniz rule d(fx) = f dx + x⊗df, extends d to the de Rham complex E⊗Ω^•, and defines curvature and integrability.

Purpose: this is the opening of a section titled 'Connexions sur torseurs affines', preliminary to Gauss–Manin. The module case is set up first, presumably to be generalized to connections on torsors under vector bundles.
errors: No mathematical errors. The sign computation f - d^1(f) = -df and the formula f(d^1_E x + ω) = d^1_E(fx) + fω - x⊗df are consistent, and they correctly give the Leibniz rule derived on the next page.
Minor notational inconsistency: (5) writes d_E, while (6) and what follows write d^0_E. Both d^{(1)}_E and d^1_E are used for the same map.

ideas.what: Connection on E relative to T defined as an O_S-linear splitting of the first-order jet (principal parts) sequence
ideas.modern_name: Connection via principal parts / Atiyah-type extension; Atiyah class as obstruction
ideas.usually_credited_to: Atiyah (1957, complex-analytic); Grothendieck, EGA IV §16 and 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (1966/68); Katz, Berthelot
ideas.where_published: EGA IV 16.7 (principal parts); Dix exposés, 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (connections/stratifications via P^n)

ideas.what: Comparison of the O_S-linear splitting with the additive universal splitting d^1_E, giving a Leibniz-rule operator E -> E⊗Ω^1
ideas.modern_name: Equivalence of the two definitions of connection (splitting vs. Koszul connection)
ideas.where_published: Crystals and de Rham cohomology (1968); EGA IV 16

ideas.what: Section heading announcing connections on affine torsors (torsors under vector bundles)
ideas.modern_name: Connections on affine bundles / torsors under E; related to universal vector extensions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mazur–Messing (1974), and others, in related contexts

missed.claim: The heading promises a treatment of connections on affine torsors, presumably torsors under vector bundles, in the Gauss–Manin context. This page only does the linear (module) case. Whether a genuinely torsor-theoretic treatment follows in later pages cannot be judged from here; similar ideas exist in the literature (e.g. Mazur–Messing).
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only marginal. Connections on affine torsors are known material; at most it documents Grothendieck's planned framing.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a textbook-level derivation of the equivalence between connections as O_S-linear splittings of the jet sequence and Leibniz-rule operators. It is already in EGA IV and in Grothendieck's crystals exposé. Only the heading about affine torsors hints at something slightly less standard.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'E module {+loc.[?]+} gén. libre[?] sur S' likely reads 'E module qu. coh. sur S, d'où' (quasi-cohérent).
After 'splitting O_S-linéaire' the insertion probably reads 'de (1)'.
In (3), the struck-out material is a crossed-out attempt at writing E⊗Ω_{S/T}; the kept formula is ξ = d^{(1)}_E x + ω.
In (4), the operator before 'x⊗df' is a minus sign written over a blot: (fω - x⊗df).
In (6), the blotted operator is a minus: δ_E x = d^1_E(x) - d^0_E(x).
The last line reads 'il faut expliciter la condition sur d^0_E de (5), pour que δx défini par (6), soit O_S-linéaire,'.
